new_entities.name: Metformin through early pregnancy in PCOS
aliases: metformin continued into pregnancy in PCOS
metformin in pregnant women with PCOS
new_entities.description: Use of metformin started before conception and continued into early pregnancy in women with polycystic ovary syndrome.

new_entities.name: Live birth rate
new_entities.description: The probability of delivering a live infant after a fertility treatment cycle or conception attempt.

edges.effect_quant: The newest randomized synthesis suggests at most a modest and uncertain live-birth benefit. In a 1,708-woman 2025 meta-analysis, preconception metformin continued through the first trimester was associated with a live-birth OR of 1.24 with confidence intervals crossing the null.
edges.population: women with polycystic ovary syndrome treated with metformin before conception and into early pregnancy
edges.mechanism: Metformin can improve insulin sensitivity, lower hyperinsulinemia, and dampen androgen excess, which may help ovulation, implantation stability, and early gestational physiology. The main uncertainty is that these endocrine benefits appear more consistent for miscarriage and obstetric complication reduction than for a clear, reproducible live-birth gain.
edges.summary: This is a reasonable but still non-definitive PCOS pregnancy-support edge. Metformin may improve the overall reproductive path in PCOS, yet the live-birth signal specifically remains modest and inconsistent rather than decisively proven.
edges.caveats: The literature spans preconception use, ovulation-induction contexts, and continuation or discontinuation after pregnancy confirmation. That makes timing critical, and it would be misleading to collapse all metformin-in-PCOS evidence into a universal live-birth claim.
